summary:
For the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, our team developed Space Life, an innovative, offline-first AI-powered web application designed to monitor and assess astronaut health parameters in deep space environments where reliable internet or real-time mission control connection is unavailable.

What we developed & how it addresses the challenge: We built a robust platform that leverages artificial intelligence locally to track vital signs, analyze health metrics, and provide instant predictive insights to astronauts. By operating entirely offline, it ensures continuous, secure, and autonomous medical oversight during deep-space missions or communication blackouts.

Why it is important: Crew safety and autonomy are paramount for long-duration space exploration. Space Life bridges the critical gap in space medicine by offering proactive, real-time health intelligence right on-site, empowering astronauts to manage potential health risks independently and ensuring mission success far from Earth.
details:
Space Life is an innovative, offline-first AI-powered web application designed to monitor, analyze, and assess astronaut health parameters in deep space environments where reliable internet or real-time mission control connection is unavailable.

1. What does it do & How does it work?

The platform operates locally using edge AI to track vital signs, log physiological metrics, and process health data without requiring cloud connectivity. It continuously monitors astronaut health parameters and uses predictive algorithms to flag early warning signs of medical anomalies, providing instant, actionable insights directly on-site during deep-space missions or communication blackouts.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Autonomous Operations: Ensures continuous medical oversight even when communication with Earth is completely severed.
  • Proactive Health Management: Identifies potential health risks before they escalate into critical emergencies.
  • Data Security & Privacy: Keeps sensitive crew health data stored locally and securely.

3. What is the intended impact?

The primary impact is enhancing crew safety, autonomy, and psychological well-being during long-duration space missions, Mars expeditions, or extended orbital stays. By bridging the critical gap in space medicine, Space Life empowers astronauts to manage their health independently and ensures mission success far from Earth.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software were used?

  • Languages & Frameworks: Modern web technologies (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, Python) for building a responsive, lightweight, and fast offline interface.
  • AI & Software: Local machine learning and edge AI models for predictive health analysis and anomaly detection.
  • Development Tools: Git/GitHub for version control and collaborative team workflow.

5. How is your project creative?

Unlike traditional health-monitoring systems that heavily rely on constant cloud syncing and active telemetry links with mission control, Space Life flips the paradigm by bringing intelligence directly to the edge. Its offline-first architecture ensures that astronauts are never left without medical intelligence, regardless of deep-space communication delays or signal blackouts.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • Reliability in Extreme Conditions: Ensuring the application remains fully functional without an active internet connection.
  • User Experience (UX): Designing a clean, intuitive interface that astronauts can easily navigate under high-stress or fatigue conditions.
  • Scalability & Adaptability: Creating a modular framework that can easily integrate with various wearable health sensors and medical datasets.
